<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/ai/tool.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **137** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2f2fa11d756f665a4c06160480c1dce15b9d67a4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c2e5b3b8146a6917038bb6647b658e29fc7ce1ee`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed as an isolated subagent on PR #21021 (card #20809), from the card's body and its three comments (the pointer, the claim, the os-dev report), the PR body, its 7-file list, the net diff against `main`, files read at the head by `git show`, and the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept set — unchanged, judged right.** The three `packages/spec/src/**` hunks are docblock text only: `shared/strict-object.ts` (the file-header bullet for `guidance` and the `StrictObjectOptions.guidance` JSDoc) and `ai/tool.zod.ts` (the docblock above `TOOL_RETIRED_KEY_GUIDANCE`). No schema shape, no guidance-table row, no `retiredKey()`, no alias and no enum moves; the card's ⛔ "no guidance table entry changes" holds. The new wording (the slot holds prescriptions for keys the shape does not declare; a key retired in place is a `retiredKey()` tombstone in the shape) matches what the slot does: an entry suppresses the rename suggestion for an undeclared spelling, and `shared/alias-integrity.test.ts` makes a guidance row for a declared key dead. `Clause-②: no` is the right declaration.

**Published surface — text only, and it does ship, judged right.** `src/shared/index.ts` re-exports `./visibility`, whose exported `VISIBILITY_STRICT_OPTIONS` is typed `StrictObjectOptions`, so the edited JSDoc reaches the `./shared` entry's bundled declarations (`dist/shared/index.d.ts` and `.d.mts`), which the package `exports` map addresses. `src/ai/tool.zod.ts` ships verbatim through `files[]` (`src/**/*.zod.ts`). Both are hover and source text, not accept-set bytes; the consequence is a changeset (see ②), not a Clause-② arm. No generated artifact is in the diff (no `json-schema/`, `api-surface/`, `liveness/` or `src/migrations/registry.ts`), which is consistent with docblock-only source changes; `Spec property liveness` and `Check Changeset` are green on the head.

**Printed remedies in `packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas.ts` (unshipped) — judged right.** Measured on the head versus the merge base `05be35259`: `grep -n -E 'migrations/registry\.ts|copy these lines|step in src/migrations'` returns 10 lines at the base and 2 at the head, both code comments (the new section header at `:771` and the existing check (a) comment at `:1162`). The ten printed sites named in the PR's H1 table are all rerouted. Each remedy that knows the id and the major prints the exact entry file plus its one declaration through `renderNewEntryFiles`; the undo remedies ((b2), (b3), def (b2)) print each registered entry's on-disk file through `retiredKeyEntryFiles` / `retiredDefEntryFiles`, which look the id up under every major and map a renamed-def carry through `carryAuthorableKey` (from `scripts/lib/renamed-defs.ts`), so the file named is the one that exists; check (c) proof 1 and the default-change remedy name the directory and `entries/README.md` because the major there is the author's to establish. Every remedy carries `MIGRATION_REGISTRY_COMMAND`, which equals the package script `gen:migration-registry` (`tsx scripts/build-migration-registry.ts`). `CURRENT_MAJOR` moved up to `:767`, after `SPEC_VERSION` (`:300`), so the earlier manifest-disappearance remedy at about `:850` can use it. The three table-naming lines left alone (`:1089` precondition, `:2619` info line, `:2781` diagnosis row) print no route and are right as they stand.

**The card's ⛔ on restating the naming convention — held.** `entryFileOf` composes `ENTRIES_DIR`, `KINDS[].dir` and `shardNameFor`, all imported from the generator; `shardNameFor` is the one rule (`MAJOR.ID.ts`, `/` and `:` to `__`) and `entries/README.md` at the head documents that same rule with the same example (`17` plus `data/AggregationNode:distinct`). The remedies name the README by its path, which exists at the head; no second prose copy of the convention was added.

**The generator `packages/spec/scripts/build-migration-registry.ts` (unshipped) — judged right.** The CLI body moved verbatim into `main(argv)` (the `--self-test` branch, the exit-when-alone rule, `--check` versus write, the stale-registry message) behind `invokedDirectly`, a realpath-on-both-sides comparison spelled byte-for-byte as the sibling `check-generated.ts` spells it (`:993-1000` there). The remaining top-level statements (`pkgRoot`, the exported path constants, `KINDS`, `closeMarker`) have no side effect, so an import runs nothing and `shardNameFor`, `KINDS`, `ENTRIES_DIR` and `type Kind` are importable, which is what `build-schemas.ts` and the check-mode test now do. Both package scripts (`gen:migration-registry`, `check:migration-registry`) run the file as `argv[1]` under tsx, so the guard answers run for them. `check:entry-guard` walks only the root `scripts/` (`ROOT_DIR_WATCH_HINTS` is `scripts/**`, held by its own self-test), so a package-local hand-typed guard is outside its population, and the dev's reason for not importing `scripts/invoked-as.mjs` (it would add a read-set input outside the `migration_registry` selector arm) is sound: that arm names `packages/spec/scripts/build-migration-registry.ts` path by path, so this PR's edit to the generator selects the scoped `check:migration-registry` step in CI.

**Tests — the card's two pins are present, judged right.** `build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts` (the `repo` vitest project, listed in `vitest.repo-tests.json`) pins gate (b) and the def-removal gate on the entry file, the `export const entry` declaration and `REGEN_COMMAND`, with `not.toContain('migrations/registry.ts')` and `not.toContain('copy these lines')` (the self-test on the message); keeps the registered-by-exact-name control; and adds the follow-the-printed-route control, which parses the file and declaration pairs off the red run, writes them into the sandbox, runs the sandbox's own generator and asserts gate (b) is then silent. `:789`, (b2), def (b2), (b3) and the unpublish repro each pin their entry file. The new `build-migration-registry-entry.test.ts` (the `local` project via `scripts/**/*.test.ts`) pins both guard directions as real tsx processes, including the symlink run. `tsconfig.scripts.json` includes `scripts/**/*`, so both scripts and the new test are in the typecheck program (`Type Check · source gates` green on the head).

**Coordination with the kit — judged right.** The PR quotes the retirement kit's section 3 as it reads on `main` (`745ac30a`, an ancestor of `origin/main`; `.claude/skills/spec-property-retirement/SKILL.md` lines 182-184): one file under `entries/retired-keys/`, naming per `entries/README.md`, then `gen:migration-registry`, never typed in `registry.ts`. The gate and the kit now say the same route, and this card landed second and quotes the first, as the card's Order section asks. No governed surface is in the diff (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green).

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/20809-guidance-slot-docblocks.md` declares `'@objectstack/spec': patch` and carries `Clause-②: no`, matching the PR body's `Clause-②: no`. Right: the diff ships text (a published declaration's JSDoc and a shipped source docblock), and `skip-changeset` is reserved for a diff that publishes nothing from any released package (AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3; the os-dev rule that published means what each package's `files[]` ships). No accept set widens or narrows, so neither `minor` nor a breaking level applies, and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. The changeset body states that no schema, guidance entry, prescription or parse behaviour changes, which the diff bears out. `Check Changeset` is green on the head. The dev's deviation from the os-dev fast path (comments as non-publishing) is the measured call, and it is the right one here.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` is empty. The five deviations and three out-of-scope findings in the os-dev report:

- **Deviation 1, landing beyond the claimed file surface (the generator's `main()` and guard, plus the new guard test).** Answered: accepted. The card's own ⛔ (no second copy of the naming rule) forces the remedies to read `shardNameFor` from the generator, and the generator ran its CLI at import, so the guard is the minimal change that makes the card's instruction satisfiable. Both files are unshipped scripts; the generator's read set is unchanged (only `realpathSync` from `node:fs` was added), and its path is already in the `migration_registry` selector arm, so CI's scoped gate covers the edit. Escalated to the seat as bookkeeping only: the claim's file surface should be amended to name `packages/spec/scripts/build-migration-registry.ts` and `packages/spec/scripts/build-migration-registry-entry.test.ts`, as the dev asked. Not blocking.
- **Deviation 2, in-place fixes beyond the named lines ((b2), (b3), def (b2), check (c) proofs 1 and 3, the default-change remedy).** Answered: accepted. The card's pointer comment already folded the def-removal gate and `:789` in; the others are the same defect (a printed remedy routing an author into the generated file), in the same file, mechanical, and each is named in the PR's H1 table with its verdict.
- **Deviation 3, `patch` instead of `skip-changeset`.** Answered in ②: `patch` is right.
- **Deviation 4, `main` not pulled before the PR.** Answered: at read the PR is mergeable against base `2f2fa11d7`, and CI runs on the merge ref (`2febc4b64`, per the docs-drift comment). The eleven intervening commits touch none of the 7 paths or `src/migrations/`. Not blocking; the seat's landing re-read of the checks covers it.
- **Deviation 5, measurement notes (the first targeted run selected nothing; one exit code read from the absence of the failure marker).** Informational; the check-runs on the head are the verdicts.
- **Out-of-scope 1, `scripts/lib/sharded-artifacts.ts` at about `:353`.** The manifest shard `description` still says "must be declared in RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR (src/migrations/registry.ts)", and `json-schema.manifest/` ships in `files[]`, so this is the same defect family on a published artifact. Leaving it out of this PR is right (the card scopes build-schemas remedies and two docblocks; the change regenerates every manifest shard). Escalated: it is recorded with carrier none, so the seat should file a follow-up card or it is lost. Not blocking.
- **Out-of-scope 2, the "Tombstones for RETIRED keys" section comment inside `src/data/object.zod.ts`'s `UNKNOWN_KEY_GUIDANCE`.** Answered: the card's ⛔ on guidance-table edits makes leaving it right; fold into the same follow-up card.
- **Out-of-scope 3, the `scripts/lib/default-changes.ts` comment at about `:52`.** Answered: an unshipped comment whose printed remedy is fixed here; fold into the same follow-up card.
